evals.prompt: We want to run evals/idiomatic-go/fixtures/orders-api on Kubernetes with several replicas. Can you check it against twelve-factor and tell me what blocks that?
evals.expected_output: Evaluate mode table covering all twelve factors. Violations: in-memory Orders map (VI), orders.log written to local disk (VI), hardcoded :8080 listen address (VII/III), no SIGTERM handling or graceful shutdown (IX). Unknown for factors the repo cannot show (V, X). Priority fixes lead with state that breaks horizontal scaling.
expectations: Uses evaluate mode and produces a per-factor table with a status for each of the twelve factors
Flags the package-level Orders map as process-local state that breaks with multiple replicas (Processes)
Flags writing orders.log to the local filesystem (Processes or Logs)
Flags the hardcoded :8080 listen address instead of a port from the environment (Port binding or Config)
Flags the absence of SIGTERM handling / graceful shutdown (Disposability)
Marks factors the repo cannot show (e.g. build/release/run, dev/prod parity) as Unknown rather than guessing
Cites file:line for every Partial or Violation
Priority fixes put the in-memory state ahead of lower-risk items
Does not drift into general Go code-quality findings (error handling style, naming) unrelated to the factors

evals.prompt: I'm designing a new notifications service: a Python HTTP API that accepts send requests, plus a worker that pulls jobs from a queue and sends email and SMS. It will run on AWS. Help me plan it twelve-factor style.
evals.expected_output: Design mode. Asks for missing facts (queue choice, datastore, deployment target such as ECS vs Lambda) or states them as assumptions, then gives a per-factor decision table naming concrete mechanisms, plus tradeoffs.
expectations: Uses design mode and produces a per-factor decision table
Asks about or explicitly flags missing facts (queue, datastore, compute platform) instead of silently assuming them
Names concrete mechanisms (e.g. specific env vars, a queue service, release-phase migrations) rather than restating the principles
Treats the API and the worker as separate process types (Concurrency)
Covers graceful shutdown for the worker, including returning or finishing in-flight jobs (Disposability)

evals.prompt: /twelve-factor-app How do I make my Go HTTP server finish in-flight requests when Kubernetes sends SIGTERM?
evals.expected_output: Direct answer: signal.NotifyContext plus http.Server.Shutdown with a timeout, with a short snippet. No full twelve-factor evaluation table and no question about which mode to use.
expectations: Answers directly with a working approach (signal.NotifyContext or signal.Notify plus http.Server.Shutdown with a timeout)
Does not produce a full twelve-factor evaluation or design table
Does not ask the user to choose between evaluate and design mode
